title: Pete Nugent's influence and a demonstration
summary: Green calls Nugent organised and versatile, an influence on film dancers from Astaire to Donald O'Connor, and demonstrates his style with travelling steps.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Let me ask you. What was it about Pete Nugent that made him so great?

Well, he was -- he was like a caliber, you know. He was always organized. Organizes. Organizes. I mean it's in his versatilities, you see. It was like seeing a student body of the learneds, you see, which was in the days of our forefathers, you see. Everything he did was memorable, you see, especially to show folk, you see. Even in the moving pictures, the studios, I mean. If you watch today's shows, you'll see more of Pete Nugent that you would of anyone, including Fred Astaire, Gene Kelly. Say like Gene Nelson, people like that, Dan Daily, and Van Johnson, Donald O'Connor and people like that, you see.
You mean his particular style influenced --
Yeah.
-- all these people?
Yes. He's like a -- what you would call -- he's an impregnator. That's why he retitled his name, you see. Public Tapper Number One, Pete Nugent, see.
I'd love to see you do something of
his.
Well, I could do some of his fragmentations. And I'd be glad I got the wind in my sails.
(Mr. Green dances)
(applauds) Bravo.
Did you like the properties?
Very much.
Beautiful. Beautiful.
(Off the record) (Recording interruption)
George, we must say first how much we noticed what a different style that is, because we noticed how much more Chuck was using the stage -- what they call using the stage more.
Yeah. Well, that's really without miniatures, you see. There's no mimicry going on there. See, they're all quotations. And that's why he encumbered any kind of description, see.
Well, I noticed there was a lot more traveling in your dancing.
Yeah. Well, traveling does encumber, you see, because it has to reinstate. Like, I said before, dads and grads. It's from one (unintelligible) to the other, you see. We must have reinstate, see.
You had all that wonderful rhythms with your feet, but you notice that there was all this lovely,
graceful movement on the stage, which I was very happy to see, as I never had the opportunity to see Pete Nugent dance. We're so lucky to have you do these things for us.
(Recording interruption)
